question: Phase 0: can the engine host, cook, stream and draw an island world with distant landscape?
world: world-cook init (island_fixture.rs): 8,192 m square of 32 m cells (65,536), 27.7 km2 of land, 762 m summit, sea level 0, 1 m heights and paint, composite minimum level 2

cook.note: source generation ~28 s plus cook; leaf composites evaluated on 12 cores; peak memory 665 MB
cook.hill_parallel_bake: hill fixture material cook 61 s -> 17 s with an identical content hash

profiles.method: yarra-app-game --render-repro landscape --profile-seconds 10 --profile-warmup 8 --profile-fps 0, 2560x1440 native, 4x MSAA, grass on, windowed; update intervals, not GPU time

terrain_lod.spawn: 511 patches / 1,046,528 triangles, budget limited, max visible error 2.4 px
terrain_lod.summit: 511 / 1,046,528, budget limited, 4.7 px (9,335 px before rounding ridge crests)

findings: Distant terrain beyond 1 km was never drawn before: Bevy's default far plane culled it. World views now cull at 20 km.

Coloured horizontal streaks in hazy distant terrain vanish with 100 km visibility and persist with clouds off: they come from the aerial-perspective transmittance segment (Bevy sample_transmittance_lut_segment on ground-hitting rays), not terrain.
Views over the whole island saturate the terrain LOD budget (512 patches, 1M triangles); the planner's pairwise checks limit raising it.
Knife-edge ridges from folded noise aliased into saw-tooth silhouettes at coarse levels; rounded crests fixed it.
The runtime file is 789 MB for 445 MB of payload: SQLite overflow pages for 1-4 KB blobs.
limitations: Single short runs, windowed, display-paced update intervals; not GPU attribution, power or sustained thermals. Grass-covered procedural island without trees, sand or rock textures.
